description: vinyl tiles made from polyvinyl chloride (PVC)
blurb: The ruling's code, 3918.10.10.00, was split into new lines after it was issued. Open the time machine.
reference_excerpt: The product in question is vinyl tiles made from polyvinyl chloride (PVC), which are classified under the Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS) as floor coverings of plastics. The specific HTS code 3918.10.1000 is applicable because it pertains to floor coverings made from polymers of vinyl chloride, which includes vinyl tiles. The tiles submitted for classification measure 12 inches square and 13 inches square, confirming they are indeed floor coverings in tile form. The ruling indicates that the applicable subheading covers such products, and the duty rate of 5.3 percent ad valorem is specified for this classification.

classification.rationale: Heading 3918 covers plastic floor coverings including vinyl tile, and PVC vinyl tiles fall under subheading 3918.10 (polymers of vinyl chloride) as 'floor coverings: vinyl tile' per GRI 1, consistent with multiple in-force CROSS rulings (N261168, N327606, N341739, N261969) classifying PVC vinyl tile/plank products there. However, the 10-digit statistical suffix turns on whether the tile has a rigid solid core, a rigid expanded core, or neither, which the description does not state, so I default to the 'Other' line but flag this as an assumption requiring confirmation.
